spec_trace.primary_anchor: 2.3.13.12 Local Account, Principal, Access Space, and Protected Resource Authority
supporting_anchors: 11.20 Shared Workspace, SaaS, and MCP Authorization Foundation
spec_trace.roadmap_pointer: Kernel reset brief Week 6 Account, Principal, Resource Authority, Access Space, and Persona/CRM Layers; Phase B.

original_intent_carried_forward: External agents, visitor passes, and MCP clients are first-class Principals with higher scrutiny.
MCP server manifests are fingerprinted and material changes trigger re-consent.
New MCP and visitor Principals are default-deny and ToolGate controls each tool action.
Visitor passes are short-lived, narrow, non-spawning, and revocable.
Operator surfaces list, scope, revoke, and visibly attribute MCP/visitor actions.
Concurrent operator/MCP isolation and immediate revocation remain required.
new_scope_added: AccessSpace, ProtectedResource, ResourceLink, ResourceGrant, MembershipRole, and ResourceBroker.
Per-resource privacy inside shared projects and explicit client/SFW/master Spaces.
Filesystem, ArtifactStore, search/index, derivative, export, backup, archive, and restore authorization.
ExternalIdentityBinding and RemoteServiceConnection seam for future Handshake SaaS/MCP.
Remote moodboard/project-starter/inspiration manifests, quarantine, local-scope selection, and provenance.
superseded_draft_assumptions: AccessSpace is not a Profile and never grants access.
Project membership is not blanket visibility.
Read-only MCP tools are not automatically safe; they can exfiltrate private data.
MCP fingerprints cover the full security-relevant surface, not only transient tool-list text.
Revocation semantics include in-flight cancellation/containment and derived/cache/context invalidation.

naming_contract.AccessSpace: named selectable context over resources already authorized by ResourceGrant
naming_contract.ProtectedResource: any primary or derived object with visibility consequences
naming_contract.ResourceLink: durable association between resource and project/workspace/client/Space without itself granting access
naming_contract.ResourceGrant: durable action authorization for a Principal/account/group/role/service/pass over an exact resource or bounded set
naming_contract.MembershipRole: project/workspace collaboration role used by policy but not blanket resource authority
naming_contract.ResourceBroker: executable filesystem and ArtifactStore authorization boundary

scope.intent: Implement exact resource visibility and sharing across accounts, Spaces, projects, files, database-backed objects, assets, artifacts, models/tools, visitors, MCP clients, and future remote services without losing the original visitor-pass and MCP scrutiny role.
in_scope: ProtectedResource kinds and stable ResourceRef taxonomy for every primary/derived boundary.
AccessSpace schema, lifecycle, membership, resource links, defaults, master/SFW/client use cases, and explicit rule that Space does not grant.
ProtectedResource registry and ownership/lineage/storage-locator envelope.
ResourceGrant schema with subject, resource/set, actions, conditions, inheritance, issue/expiry/revocation, provenance, and policy version.
Central authorization evaluator combining Principal/session, ResourceGrant, MembershipRole, AccessSpace, capability, action, policy, and revocation.
Project/workspace membership and exact resource linking without blanket project visibility.
Generalized RLS policies for resource, grant, Space, project, collaboration, index, log, and projection tables.
Authorization-query and explain APIs that do not reveal restricted existence.
ResourceBroker for registered external roots, canonical paths, symlink/junction/traversal defense, ArtifactStore handles, and post-revocation denial.
Derived resources, mixed-scope source intersection, previews/thumbnails/caches/indexes/embeddings/search/model contexts/logs/exports/backups/archive/restore.
Same-project private resources and concurrent grant/revoke/use behavior.
Authenticated-session AccessSpace pinning and atomic switching.
Collaborator invite, membership role, exact grants, revoke, and bounded recovery.
Visitor-pass issue/use/expiry/revoke, no spawn, action/resource ceiling, audit, and in-flight policy.
MCP Principal allocation, full security-surface fingerprint, re-consent, ToolGate, per-action approval, badges, and admin UI.
MCP tools/resources/prompts/sampling/elicitation/callback authorization and audience-bound token posture.
ExternalIdentityBinding and RemoteServiceConnection contract.
RemoteResourceManifest for moodboards, project starters, inspiration items, provenance/hash/deletion/visibility, quarantine, inspection, import, and local linking.
Native Space/resource/share/visitor/MCP/service UI, privacy inspector, UserManual, Argus, EventLedger, and Flight Recorder.
Real PostgreSQL, filesystem, concurrency, side-channel, revocation, export/restore, MCP, and remote-import end-to-end proof.
out_of_scope: Password/login implementation and Principal foundation owned by WP-KERNEL-006.
Persona, preferences, CRM, and FEMS personalization owned by WP-KERNEL-008.
Production SaaS backend, billing, public federation, generalized SSO, and public marketplace.

mandatory_negative_scenarios: revoked grant with open file/model/tool context
path traversal, symlink, or junction escape
backup or export restored under unauthorized account
remote import attempts automatic local publication

selected_patterns: collection/moodboard manifests separated from local authorization
rejected_patterns: remote ACL automatically becoming local grant
MCP connection inheriting logged-in human authority

activation_acceptance: WP-KERNEL-006 is implemented and Integration Validator-verified.
Refinement locks all resource kinds, grant semantics, Space behavior, membership interaction, RLS, ResourceBroker, revocation, side-channel, MCP, visitor, and remote-manifest contracts.
Refinement includes complete primary/derived resource inventory and every producer/consumer boundary.
Official packet adopts the complete pre-created MT index without silent deletion.
A new WP activation signature is obtained.

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: restricted rows are hidden in UI but retrievable through API/search/model/tool/export
risks_and_hardening.hardening: central evaluator plus RLS/Broker enforcement and negative tests at every consumer

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: coworker joins a project and sees private porn-production files or artifacts
risks_and_hardening.hardening: membership is policy input only; exact ResourceGrant required; same-project-private E2E fixture

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: thumbnail, embedding, summary, log, or export has broader visibility than source
risks_and_hardening.hardening: source-scope intersection, split/redact/refuse policy, lineage and mixed-scope tests

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: tool supplies path outside granted root through traversal/junction/symlink
risks_and_hardening.hardening: registered roots, canonical handles, revalidation, OS-specific escape tests

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: service token or remote collection grants local content access
risks_and_hardening.hardening: separate Principal/audience/grant, quarantine imports, explicit local destination and publication grants

microtasks.adoption_rule: Activation Manager must compare refinement/packet scope to every pre-created MT, preserve each original visitor/MCP and resource-privacy obligation, record any split/merge/supersession, validate the DAG, and activate no more than one MT at a time.

minimum_controls: No product implementation may begin from this stub or its inactive MTs.
Refinement must prove backend enforcement for every resource boundary, not only UI visibility.
Same-project private resources, concurrent revocation, side-channel denial, and remote import quarantine are mandatory scenarios.
